name: Jordan Ellis, IMCU: insulin pump failure and moderate DKA

caseMeta.title: Intermediate care to medical floor: insulin pump failure after a weekend of drinking, moderate DKA in a young adult with type 1 diabetes (3 days, checkpoints at every 0700 and 1900)
learningObjectives: Explain why an insulin pump user (rapid-acting insulin only, no long-acting depot) can go into DKA within hours of an infusion set failure, and recognize DKA hidden behind "a hangover" (vomiting, belly pain, deep fast breathing).

Manage an adult DKA protocol (2024 consensus) safely: isotonic/balanced fluids, fixed-rate insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h, a dextrose line when glucose is under 250, potassium rules with peripheral limits (hold insulin when K is under 3.5), magnesium, and the resolution criteria.

Carry out the transition with basal insulin 1-2 hours before stopping the drip, and the pump restart only after endocrinology and the diabetes educator review; prevent and treat hypoglycemia after the transition.

Teach pump troubleshooting (site checks, the unexplained-high rule: ketones, pen injection, set change), sick-day rules for pump users, backup pens and long-acting insulin, CGM alarms, and safer drinking with type 1 diabetes; screen for alcohol withdrawal and give a brief alcohol intervention.

orders.name: lactated Ringer's 1,000 mL with potassium chloride 20 mEq/L (main DKA fluid)
orders.instructions: Run at 250 mL/h through the left forearm 18 g IV. When the dextrose 10% line starts (glucose under 250), lower this bag to 100 mL/h (total about 200 mL/h). K 3.5-5.0 = KCl 20 mEq/L in the lactated Ringer's (never more than 20 mEq/L in a peripheral bag). K under 3.5 = HOLD the insulin infusion, call the provider, give KCl 10 mEq/100 mL riders over 1 hour each through the second IV (no more than 10 mEq per hour peripherally; up to 4 in a row), recheck K after every 20 mEq, restart insulin when K is 3.5 or higher.
orders.rationale: K 4.6 at 0300 and voiding: KCl 20 mEq/L (adult rule for K 3.5-5.0). 250 mL/h = 3.5 mL/kg/h; 5 mEq K per hour.

orders.name: insulin regular (HUMULIN R) 100 units in 0.9% sodium chloride 100 mL (1 unit/mL) infusion - DKA (fixed rate)

Independent double check at every bag/rate change. FIXED RATE: do not lower it for a falling glucose; use the dextrose 10% line instead. HOLD and call if potassium is under 3.5. Call for glucose under 150 on D10 150 mL/h, a fall of more than 100 mg/dL in 1 hour, or glucose under 70. Continue unchanged on transfer to the IMCU.

notes.author: J. Whitaker, RN
notes.summary: Arrived 0030 with his roommate: vomiting all day Sunday after a weekend of drinking; insulin pump set found pulled half out. Deep fast breathing, fruity breath. POC glucose 556. ESI 2.
notes.body:
**Arrival 0030** by private car with his roommate (Theo Grant), who found him "breathing weird and not making sense" when he got home from work at about 2345.

**Story (Jordan and roommate)**
- Type 1 diabetes since age 11, on a tubed insulin pump with a CGM.
- Saturday night: friend's birthday, about 10-12 drinks (beer and shots) from about 2100 to 0200, ate little. Fell asleep on a friend's couch in his clothes; his phone died, so he did not hear CGM alarms.
- Sunday: woke about 1000, vomiting from about 1100 ("8-10 times"), belly ache, thought it was a hangover. CGM high all day; gave two correction boluses through the pump (about 1300 and 1700). Did not check ketones (no strips at home). No backup insulin pen that works and no long-acting insulin at home.
- No fever, cough or diarrhea. Denies drugs. Allergy: penicillin (hives as a child).

**Triage 0035**
T 99.0 F, HR 122, BP 104/62, RR 28 deep and regular (Kussmaul), SpO2 98% room air, pain 5/10 upper belly, headache 3/10. Weight 72.0 kg (bed scale). Sleepy but answers; GCS 15. Fruity (acetone) breath, no smell of alcohol. Dry mouth.

**Insulin pump**: infusion set on the left lower abdomen half pulled off; adhesive lifted and wet; insulin smell on the dressing; tubing twisted around his belt loop.

**POC glucose 0040: 556.**

ESI 2. To room 12; Dr. Castillo at the bedside 0040. DKA order set.

notes.title: ED Provider Note - Moderate DKA, Insulin Pump Failure
notes.author: R. Castillo, MD
notes.summary: 24-year-old with type 1 diabetes on an insulin pump: moderate DKA (pH 7.22, bicarbonate 10, gap 26, BHB 6.2) after an infusion set failure during a weekend of binge drinking. Ethanol none detected; lipase normal. Adult protocol started; admit to IMCU.
notes.body:
**Chief complaint**
Vomiting all day, belly pain, fast breathing.

**HPI**
Type 1 diabetes for 13 years on a tubed insulin pump with CGM (last HbA1c 7.4% in October, per patient). Saturday night: about 10-12 drinks, little food, slept in his clothes on a friend's couch. The infusion set (placed Thursday) caught on his belt: cannula half out and bent. Phone dead overnight, so no CGM alarms. Sunday: vomiting from about 1100, which he blamed on a hangover; two pump corrections that did not work; no ketone check; no backup pen. Roommate brought him in.

**Exam (0040)**
HR 122, BP 104/62, RR 28 Kussmaul, SpO2 98%, T 99.0 F. Sleepy, GCS 15, oriented. Fruity breath. Dry mucosa. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mild diffuse tenderness, no peritoneal signs. No tremor. Pump site left lower abdomen: no cellulitis.

**Results**
- 0045: glucose 572, Na 133 (corrected about 141), **K 5.4**, Cl 97, **CO2 10, anion gap 26**, BUN 24, **creatinine 1.4** (baseline 0.9), Mg 1.9, phos 5.2. **BHB 6.2. VBG pH 7.22, pCO2 24, HCO3 9.4** (Winter's expected 20-24: appropriate compensation). Lactate 2.6.
- Measured osmolality 309; calculated 306 (osmolal gap 3: no toxic alcohol). **Ethanol none detected**, acetaminophen and salicylate negative. Lipase 48. AST 46, ALT 39, GGT 68. WBC 15.8 (typical of DKA), Hgb 16.2.
- UA: glucose 4+, ketones large, no infection. Urine drug screen negative. Respiratory PCR negative.
- ECG 0115: sinus tach 118, tall T waves, no arrhythmia.
- 0300: glucose 470, **K 4.6**, CO2 11, gap 23, BHB 5.6, pH 7.25.

**Assessment**
**Moderate DKA** (pH 7.00-7.24, bicarbonate 10-15, alert) from **insulin pump infusion set failure**; alcohol, vomiting and fasting made it worse and hid it. **Alcoholic ketoacidosis** was considered (binge, vomiting, starvation) but glucose 572 with a failed pump points to DKA; some overlap is possible and is treated the same way (fluids, dextrose, insulin, thiamine). Prerenal AKI. No infection found.

**Plan (adult DKA protocol, ADA/EASD/JBDS/AACE/DTS 2024 consensus)**
1. Normal saline 1 L over the first hour (done), then lactated Ringer's 500 mL/h x2 h, then 250 mL/h.
2. **Insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h = 7.2 units/h, fixed rate, no bolus**, started 0215 once K was known to be over 3.5.
3. **Potassium**: none while K over 5.0; **KCl 20 mEq/L from 0400** (K 4.6, voiding). Peripheral IVs only.
4. Dextrose 10% line when glucose is under 250; keep insulin running until pH 7.3+ (or bicarbonate 18+) and BHB under 0.6.
5. Thiamine given. CIWA-Ar monitoring. Ondansetron.
6. Pump suspended; stays off until endocrinology reviews.
7. Admit IMCU (hospital medicine, Dr. Raman accepting).

notes.title: IMCU Admission History and Physical
notes.author: P. Raman, MD
notes.summary: Admit to IMCU: moderate DKA in type 1 diabetes after insulin pump set failure during a binge-drinking weekend. Fixed-rate insulin, LR with KCl 20, D10 line when glucose under 250, peripheral potassium limits, CIWA-Ar, endocrinology consult.
notes.body:
**Chief complaint**
Vomiting and fast breathing; insulin pump set pulled out.

**HPI**
See ED note. In the ED: normal saline 1 L, LR 500 mL/h x2 h, then LR with KCl 20 mEq/L at 250 mL/h; insulin 7.2 units/h since 0215 (no bolus); ondansetron, thiamine.

**Past history**
Type 1 diabetes diagnosed at 11 (DKA at diagnosis; no DKA since). Pump since age 14, CGM since 16. Adult endocrinology since 19 (last visit 10/06/2026, HbA1c then 7.4%). No retinopathy, kidney disease or neuropathy known. No surgeries. Immunizations up to date including influenza (October).

**Medicines (home)**
Insulin lispro by pump only (basal about 21.6 units/day; carbohydrate ratio 1:10; correction 1:45 to target 120). **No long-acting insulin at home; his only lispro pen expired in 2025.** No ketone strips.

**Allergies**: penicillin (hives as a child).

**Social history**
Line cook at a downtown restaurant (afternoon/evening shifts; eats a staff meal). Lives with a roommate (Theo Grant). Alcohol: binge drinking 2-3 nights a month (6-12 drinks), none daily, no morning drinking, no past withdrawal or seizures. Never smoked; occasional vaping; denies drugs. Insured on his parents' plan. Parents (Karen and Mark) live 3 hours away.

**Exam (0600)**
HR 106, BP 112/68, RR 24 deep, SpO2 98% RA, T 98.8 F. Awake, oriented, GCS 15. No tremor, no sweating. Fruity breath. Mucosa dry. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, mild upper tenderness. Old pump site clean. CGM on the right arm.

**Results**
ED panels 0045 and 0300 (see ED note). POC glucose 316 at 0600. 0630 labs pending.

**Assessment**
24-year-old man with **moderate DKA** from **insulin pump infusion set failure** (no long-acting insulin on board, so ketones built up within hours), made worse by binge drinking and vomiting; prerenal AKI; improving (gap 26 to 23).

**Plan**
1. **DKA**: insulin 7.2 units/h fixed; **dextrose 10% line at 100 mL/h when glucose is under 250** (LR down to 100 mL/h); D10 rate by glucose (table in the order). BMP, Mg, phos, VBG, BHB every 4 h. Resolution: pH 7.3+ (or bicarbonate 18+) AND BHB under 0.6.
2. **Potassium**: KCl 20 mEq/L in LR (peripheral maximum 20 mEq/L). **K under 3.5: hold insulin, call, KCl 10 mEq riders over 1 h each (10 mEq/h maximum peripherally)**. Magnesium per labs.
3. **Alcohol**: CIWA-Ar every 4 h until 72 h after the last drink (Wed 0200); lorazepam only for CIWA 10+ after a low glucose is ruled out. Thiamine daily. Brief intervention by social work.
4. **Pump**: off until endocrinology and the diabetes educator review; his CGM may stay on (trends only).
5. NPO except ice chips and sips (vomiting); advance when nausea settles.
6. Monitor, VS hourly, strict I&O, daily weight. Full Code.

- 0100 ondansetron 4 mg IV. 0105 thiamine 100 mg IV (before any dextrose).
- 0115 ECG: sinus tach 118, tall T waves (K 5.4). Void 450 mL (urine sample and drug screen).
- 0130 vomited 200 mL clear.

- Vitals 0615: HR 106, BP 112/68, RR 24 (less deep), SpO2 98%, T 98.8 F. GCS 15, more awake. CIWA-Ar 2 at 0130 (nausea, mild headache), no tremor.

Embarrassed ("I know better"). Asking for his pump back and for food and a soda: told the pump stays off while the IV insulin runs, and only ice chips and sips of water for now. Roommate went home at 0300; mother (Karen Ellis) updated by phone with his permission.

notes.title: Endocrinology Consult - DKA After Insulin Pump Failure
notes.author: M. Feld, MD
notes.summary: Pump-failure DKA in a well-controlled pump user (A1c 7.6%): no long-acting insulin depot, so ketones in hours. Alcohol hid the warning signs. Plan: finish IV insulin; glargine bridge before the drip stops; restart the pump only after a pump review with the diabetes educator.
notes.body:
**Reason for consult**
Type 1 diabetes on an insulin pump, DKA.

**History**
Diagnosed at 11; pump since 14; CGM since 16. HbA1c **7.6%** today (7.4% in October). No DKA since diagnosis. Infusion set changed every 3 days (abdomen only; some lumpy areas). Never had a site fail like this before. No backup pens or long-acting insulin at home, no ketone strips; has not had a sick-day plan review since moving to adult care.

**Results**
Gap 26 (0045) to 18 (1030). BHB 6.2 to 3.1. pH 7.27, CO2 14 at 1030. **K 3.8**, Mg 1.9 after 2 g, phos 2.2. Glucose 186-198 on the D10 line.

**Assessment**
1. **DKA from interrupted insulin delivery.** A pump gives only rapid-acting insulin; when delivery stops, there is no long-acting insulin left after about 2-4 hours and ketones climb fast. His A1c is good, which shows that DKA in a pump user is about **delivery**, not overall control.
2. **Alcohol**: drinking lowers glucose (the liver stops releasing glucose) and adds starvation ketosis; vomiting "from a hangover" hid DKA. Alcoholic ketoacidosis may have added to the ketones, but the glucose (572) and the failed set make this DKA.
3. **Phosphorus and potassium** falling as expected on insulin.

**Recommendations**
1. Continue fixed-rate insulin 7.2 units/h and the dextrose line until **pH 7.3+ (or bicarbonate 18+) AND BHB under 0.6**. Do not stop for a normal glucose.
2. Potassium per protocol; keep magnesium 2 or higher.
3. **Transition** once resolved and eating: **glargine 20 units** (about 90% of his pump basal) 2 hours before the drip stops; lispro 1 unit/10 g with meals + correction 1 unit/45 above 150.

notes.title: Hospital Medicine Night Event Note - Potassium 3.3, Insulin Held
notes.author: P. Raman, MD
notes.summary: K 3.3 at 1830 (resulted 1915) with flat T waves and U waves: insulin infusion HELD 1920, D10 off, KCl 10 mEq riders x4 (10 mEq/h), magnesium 2 g. STAT BMP 2130. Restart insulin when K 3.5 or higher.
notes.body:
**Called by RN at 1918** for K 3.3 (critical trend).

**Results 1830**
Na 139, **K 3.3** (after 20 mEq of riders 1600-1800), Cl 108, CO2 16, **gap 15**, BUN 13, Cr 0.9, **Mg 1.7**, phos 1.8, **BHB 1.8**, pH 7.31, pCO2 31. Glucose 192 at 1900.

**Bedside 1925**
Awake, talking, no weakness or cramps, no palpitations. Monitor: sinus 90s, **T waves flat with U waves**. ECG 1935: sinus 92, flat T, U waves V2-V3, QTc 468, no arrhythmia.

**Assessment**
Hypokalemia from insulin moving potassium into cells, plus urine losses and low-normal magnesium (alcohol). Adult protocol: **K under 3.5 = hold insulin and replace potassium first** (insulin would drive K lower and risk arrhythmia).

**Plan**
1. **Insulin infusion HELD at 1920.** D10 line stopped at the same time (no dextrose without insulin). LR + KCl 20 continues at 100 mL/h.
2. **KCl 10 mEq/100 mL over 1 h x4** (1930, 2030, 2130, 2230) through the right antecubital IV, one at a time (peripheral maximum 10 mEq/h). Total K now about 12 mEq/h with the LR.
3. **Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV** over 1 h (1930).
4. **STAT BMP, Mg, VBG, BHB at 2130.** Restart insulin 7.2 units/h as soon as K is 3.5 or higher, and the D10 line at 100 mL/h if glucose is under 250.
5. POC glucose hourly (206 at 2000). Ketones may rise a little while insulin is off: keep the hold as short as possible.
6. Cardiac monitor; call for ectopy, K under 3.0, or glucose over 300.

notes.title: Endocrinology Progress Note - Transition to Subcutaneous Insulin
notes.author: M. Feld, MD
notes.summary: DKA resolved at 0530. Glargine 20 units at 0730 (bridge), breakfast lispro 0800, drip and D10 off 0930. Pump NOT restarted today: restart Wednesday after the educator's site-change teach-back, timed to the glargine wearing off.

**Data**
Resolved at 0530: pH 7.36, bicarbonate 20, BHB 0.4, gap 11. K 4.1. Glucose 160-166 on D10. Wants to eat.

**Discussion with Jordan**
He wants the pump back on now ("I've done this for 10 years, I can just put a new set in"). Explained: (1) he has had no basal insulin except the drip, so the switch must overlap; (2) the pump failed silently once and we need to see the whole site routine and his backup plan first; (3) a long-acting dose today means restarting the pump tomorrow morning when it wears off. He agreed, reluctantly.

**Plan**
1. **Insulin glargine 20 units SC at 0730** (pump basal 21.6 units/day; about 90%). One bridge dose only.
2. **Lispro pen with meals: 1 unit/10 g carbohydrate + correction 1 unit/45 above 150** (whole units). Bedtime correction only if over 250. If nausea returns or he may not finish the tray, dose right after eating.
3. **Stop the insulin infusion and D10 at 0930** (2 hours after glargine, after the breakfast lispro). LR + KCl 20 at 100 mL/h until 1400, then lock.
4. POC before meals, bedtime, 0300 and 1030. Rebound BMP + BHB 1130.
5. **Pump restart Wednesday about 0800-0830** after the diabetes educator watches him do a complete site change (teach-back) and the pump agreement is signed; no glargine Wednesday.
6. Dietitian today; diabetes educator today and tomorrow.

notes.title: Diabetes Education Session 1 - What Went Wrong With the Pump
notes.author: L. Abernathy, RN, CDCES
notes.summary: Reviewed the event with Jordan: dislodged set, silent phone, no ketone check, corrections through a failed set, no backup insulin. Taught the unexplained-high rule and pump-user sick-day rules. Site change teach-back planned for Wednesday 0800.
notes.body:
**What happened (his words, then the pump and CGM history)**
- Set placed Thursday, left lower abdomen, his usual spot (some lumps from overuse).
- Saturday night: drinking, asleep on a couch in jeans; tubing caught on his belt; cannula pulled half out. **No occlusion alarm**: the pump kept "delivering" onto his skin.
- Phone died: no CGM high alarms overnight.
- Sunday: high all day and vomiting; he blamed a hangover; two corrections **through the same set**; no ketone check (no strips); no pen or long-acting insulin at home.

**Teaching (teach-back for each)**
1. **Unexplained-high rule**: glucose over 250 that does not drop 1 hour after a pump correction (or any ketones, nausea or vomiting) = check blood ketones, **give the correction by PEN, change the whole set at a new site**, recheck in 1-2 hours. Never correct twice through a set you do not trust.
2. **Why pump users get DKA fast**: only rapid-acting insulin; no insulin on board 2-4 hours after delivery stops.
3. **Vomiting is DKA until proven otherwise** in type 1 diabetes, even after drinking: check ketones.
4. **Sick-day rules for pump users**: check glucose every 2-3 h and ketones every 2-4 h; never stop basal; fluids 250 mL every hour; ketones 0.6-1.4 = pen correction + set change + call if not falling; 1.5-2.9 = call now; 3.0 or more or vomiting/belly pain/fast breathing = ED.
5. **Backup kit**: long-acting pen (glargine), rapid pen, pen needles, ketone strips, spare sets and reservoirs, glucagon. Written backup plan if the pump is off for more than 2-3 hours.
6. **Site care**: rotate sites (abdomen, flank, upper buttock, thighs); avoid lumps (lipohypertrophy: poor absorption); route tubing away from belts; change every 2-3 days.

He was open and quiet: "I've never thought about the pump just... not working." Plan: **site change teach-back Wednesday 0800** with endocrinology present; CGM alarms and alcohol tomorrow.

notes.title: Transfer Summary - IMCU to 4 East
notes.author: A. Lindqvist, MD
notes.summary: Transfer to 4E-21 at 1400. No rebound ketones (BHB 0.3, gap 11 at 1130). Glucose 246 before lunch (expected rise after the drip): lunch lispro 10 units. Pump restart Wednesday with the educator.
notes.body:
**Hospital course**
Moderate DKA (pH 7.22, gap 26, BHB 6.2) from insulin pump set failure during a binge-drinking weekend. Adult protocol: 2 L crystalloid in the first 3 hours, then LR with KCl 20; fixed-rate insulin 7.2 units/h from Monday 0215; D10 line from 0805. Magnesium 1.5 replaced (2 g x2). **K 3.3 Monday evening: insulin held 1920-2200**, KCl riders 60 mEq total, ECG flat T/U waves. Resolved Tuesday 0530. Glargine 20 units 0730; drip off 0930.

**Today**
1130 labs: Na 138, K 3.9, CO2 22, **gap 11**, Cr 0.9, Mg 1.9, phos 2.8, **BHB 0.3** (no rebound). POC glucose 188 (1030), **246 (1130)**: lunch 80 g, lispro 8 + 2 = **10 units** at 1200.

**For 4 East**
- Vital signs every 4 h. POC AC/HS and 0300.
- Lispro pen meal + correction doses (orders). **Dose after the meal if he is not sure he will eat it.**
- Pump stays in the belongings bag until endocrinology restarts it Wednesday.
- CIWA-Ar every 4 h until Wednesday 0200 (all 0-1 so far).
- One IV (left forearm) saline-locked at 1400.
- Social work, dietitian and educator are seeing him.

notes.title: Social Work Assessment - Alcohol Screening and Brief Intervention
notes.author: R. Halvorsen, LCSW
notes.summary: AUDIT-C 7 (positive for risky drinking); no signs of dependence. Brief intervention done; he chose goals (no more than 3-4 drinks on a night out, eat first, tell a friend, alarms on). Roommate supportive. Work note given. Insured on his parents' plan.
notes.body:
**Situation**
Roommate Theo Grant (a coworker at another restaurant) found him and drove him in. Parents in another city, supportive; mother called daily. Line cook, 4-5 shifts a week (1400-2300); staff meal on shift; food at home fine. Insured on his parents' plan until he turns 26 (March 2028).

**Alcohol screening (SBIRT)**
- **AUDIT-C 7** (drinking 2-4 times a month = 2; 7-9 drinks on a typical drinking day = 3; 6 or more drinks monthly = 2). Positive for risky drinking (men 4 or more).
- No daily drinking, no morning drinking, no blackouts other than Saturday, no withdrawal, no legal problems. CIWA-Ar 0-1 throughout.

**Brief intervention (FRAMES)**
Feedback: the DKA started on a drinking night; alcohol hides lows and highs and stops him hearing alarms. He said "that's on me." Readiness to change 7/10. **His goals**: no more than 3-4 drinks on a night out, eat carbs first, set a bedtime glucose check, leave the CGM alarm on loud and phone charged, tell one friend what DKA looks like, never sleep in his jeans with the pump on. Information on community resources given; declined counseling referral for now; primary care follow-up.

**Plan**
Work note for this week. Roommate to know the warning signs (vomiting + high glucose = ketones and ED). No other needs.

notes.title: Nutrition Assessment - Carbohydrate Counting, Alcohol, Work Meals
notes.author: K. Osei, RD
notes.summary: Accurate carbohydrate counter. Main issues: irregular meals on a line-cook schedule and drinking without food. Taught alcohol rules (eat carbs, do not bolus for most alcohol, bedtime snack, delayed lows up to 24 h).
notes.body:
**Intake**
Usual: late breakfast, staff meal 1630, snacks at the line, late-night food after shifts. Counts carbohydrate well (tested 5 foods: within 10 g). Weight 74.2 kg today (usual 74.5).

**Teaching**
- **Alcohol**: the liver stops releasing glucose while it clears alcohol, so lows can come 6-24 hours later (overnight and the next morning). Eat a carbohydrate meal before and while drinking; do not bolus for most beer/mixer carbs on a night out (or bolus only part) because of the delayed low; bedtime snack with protein if glucose under 150; set an alarm or CGM alert for the night; check on waking. Beer and mixed drinks have carbs; spirits and dry wine have little.
- **Shift work**: bolus for the staff meal before eating, not after the rush; keep glucose tabs and a snack at the station.
- **Sick days**: if he cannot eat, keep basal and sip 15 g carbohydrate every hour (juice, regular soda) to allow insulin.

Talked through today's dinner: if unsure he will eat it all, dose after eating.

notes.title: Diabetes Education Session 2 - Site Change Teach-Back, Pump Restart, CGM Alarms, Alcohol Plan

notes.summary: Jordan did a full infusion set change with correct technique (teach-back passed) and restarted his pump at 0815. Breakfast bolus 6.4 units by the pump. Reviewed CGM alarm settings, backup plan, ketone meter, sick-day and alcohol rules.
notes.body:
**Site change teach-back (0800, Dr. Feld present)**
Hand hygiene; new reservoir filled with lispro, air bubbles removed; tubing primed until drops at the tip; new site **right lower abdomen** (2 inches from the navel, no lumps); skin cleaned and dry; set inserted; cannula filled (0.3 unit for a 6 mm soft cannula); tubing looped and taped away from the belt line; old site checked. **Pump basal resumed 0815.** All steps correct without prompts.

**Breakfast 0830**
Glucose 138 (0730). 60 g: pump calculator 60/10 = 6.0 + correction (138-120)/45 = 0.4 = **6.4 units**, given by Jordan; RN checked and documented.

**Teaching (teach-back)**
- **Check the site** at every glucose check and before bed: tubing connected, no wetness or insulin smell, no redness, cannula not kinked. Check glucose 2 hours after every set change.
- **Unexplained high**: over 250, not down 1 hour after a pump correction = ketones, pen correction, new set at a new site.
- **CGM**: urgent low alarm on and loud; high alert on (250) with repeat; phone charged and not on Do Not Disturb at night; share alerts with his roommate (he agreed).
- **Backup kit and plan**: glargine pen (20 units if the pump is off for more than about 3 hours and cannot be fixed; restart the pump 24 hours later), lispro pen, pen needles, ketone meter and strips, spare sets; nasal glucagon (roommate shown how).
- **Alcohol**: eat first, lower or skip boluses for alcohol carbs, bedtime glucose 150 or higher with a snack, temporary basal reduction overnight (about 20%) after heavy drinking per his endocrinologist, never sleep with the pump tubing tangled in clothes; a sober friend who knows the plan.

notes.title: Hospital Medicine Night Event Note - Unexplained High on the Pump (Kinked Cannula)
notes.author: P. Raman, MD
notes.summary: Glucose 276 at 2300 after pizza; pump correction 3.45 units; 298 at 0010 (no fall) with ketones 0.6. Jordan followed the rule himself: pen correction 3 units, new set at a new site (old cannula kinked). Recheck 0130 and 0300.
notes.body:
**Events (Wednesday evening)**
- 1730 glucose 204: skipped the tray (roommate bringing food); pump correction only.
- 1930 two slices of pizza (about 75 g): pump bolus 7.5 units. 2100 glucose 212.
- **2300 CGM high alert; fingerstick 276.** Pump correction (276-120)/45 = **3.45 units** at 2305.
- **0010 glucose 298**: no fall 1 hour after the correction. Pizza can cause a late rise, but **blood ketones 0.6** = insulin is not getting in.

**Action (Jordan led it; RN watched)**
- **Lispro by pen 3 units at 0020** (hospital scale (298-150)/45 = 3.3 -> 3; some pump insulin may still absorb).
- **Set changed at 0030** to the left upper buttock (flank). The old soft cannula came out **kinked** at the tip (bent on insertion or when he lay on it). No occlusion alarm had sounded.
- Water 240 mL.

**Assessment**
Exactly the failure that caused this admission, caught early this time: ketones only 0.6, no symptoms.

**Plan**
Recheck glucose at 0130 and glucose + ketones at 0300; call if ketones 1.0 or higher or glucose still over 250. Discharge plan unchanged if this settles.

notes.title: Endocrinology Note - Discharge Readiness
notes.author: M. Feld, MD
notes.summary: Ready for discharge on his pump with a backup plan. He handled a kinked-cannula high overnight correctly (ketones, pen, new set). Clinic Monday 12/21.
notes.body:
**Summary**
Moderate DKA from a dislodged pump set during a binge-drinking weekend; resolved about 27 hours after the insulin infusion started; one potassium hold; glargine bridge; one post-transition low; pump restarted after a site-change teach-back; a kinked-cannula high handled correctly overnight (pen correction and set change, ketones 0.6 to 0.2).

**Discharge plan**
- Pump settings unchanged. Change sets every 2-3 days; rotate sites; check glucose 2 hours after every set change.
- **Unexplained high** over 250 not down in 1 hour = ketones, pen, new set. Ketones 1.5+ or vomiting = call/ED.
- **Backup**: glargine 20 units if the pump is off more than about 3 hours and cannot be fixed (pump basal restarts 24 hours later); lispro pen for meals and corrections meanwhile.
- **Alcohol**: his own goals (social work); bedtime glucose and snack; CGM alarms loud; roommate knows the signs and the nasal glucagon.
- Clinic Monday 12/21; educator call Friday.
